pivotal_result: In a randomised, placebo and active-controlled trial in 135 subjects with painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (NCT02215252), PF-05089771 150 mg twice daily over 4 weeks gave a mean posterior difference in average pain score versus placebo of -0.41 (90% credible interval -1.00 to 0.17), which was not statistically significant and did not meet the predefined efficacy criterion of an effect more than 0.5 units better than placebo; the active comparator pregabalin gave -0.53 (90% credible interval -0.91 to -0.20). As predefined efficacy criteria were not met, the study did not proceed to the second part. PF-05089771 was well tolerated. Paper DOI 10.1097/j.pain.0000000000001227, Pain, August 2018.
reason_class: Failed predefined efficacy criterion in Phase II
